title: Chinese UAP task force reported in South China Morning Post

tellings.quote: Do note in the South China Morning post, I want to say it was June 2021 and they had an article like, Oh yeah, we have a UAP task force too.
in fact China had a couple years ago in the China Morning Sun an article about the five continents initiative
tellings.difference: Calls the effort the 'five continents initiative' and the paper the 'China Morning Sun', with no date beyond 'a couple years ago'; Grusch's telling puts it in June 2021 and calls it a UAP task force.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe a Chinese newspaper article from a few years back reporting a Chinese state UAP effort. 'China Morning Sun' looks like a garbled South China Morning Post.

plain: China set up its own team to study UAP, the government term for UFOs, and said so openly in a newspaper. That is the claim told on the podcast. A former intelligence officer named David Grusch, who says he was told about secret programs that recover crashed craft, points to an article in the South China Morning Post newspaper. He dates it to "June 2021" and says its message was "Oh yeah, we have a UAP task force too." Luis Elizondo, the former head of a small Pentagon office that studied unexplained aerial reports, tells it separately. He remembers it a little differently: he calls the paper "the China Morning Sun", dates it only to "a couple years ago", and says the article was about something called "the five continents initiative". Both bring it up to suggest that the United States is not the only power quietly studying the subject.
